parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hi, Scott. Here are my notes. Let's sort this presentation out, then. The first thing I found out about Stone Point is it's an extinct volcanic cone. You probably know that already, being a New Zealander.

Yes, and there are two other cones nearby, which also overlook the harbour.

Right.

Yeah, the first settlers of New Zealand, the Maori, sailed to New Zealand thousands of years after these volcanoes erupted. I think the tutor allocated us this topic, though, because of Stone Point's significant historical role, it's been used by both Maori and European settlers as a place to shelter from attack, or launch an attack, for centuries.

Yeah, and the fact it was an ideal place for building a village, it would have been quite a sheltered spot.

I suppose the Maori settled there because they thought the volcanic soil would help their crops grow.

Well, they would have realised the benefits of the soil after a few good harvests. But initially the fishing opportunities would have been the attraction.

You're right.

Actually, I also read that Maori regard Stone Point as taonga. I believe it means a treasured thing.

Wow, your Māori vocabulary is improving, Scott. Hmm. We do have to deal with Stone Point's cultural value for Māori. That's still part of its historical significance. But we need to keep most Maori terminology out of the presentation. Otherwise, a lot of the international students won't be able to follow us.

That's a shame. I'm sure they'd be interested. I mean, I am. But, yeah, we wouldn't be able to explain it in the time allowed so I guess we have to stick to English. Anyway, European migrants turned Stone Point into a lookout point for ships. Then it became a fort, an army base in the late 1880s, and then during the World Wars the fort was modernised again.

It's also been a public park sometimes.

I'd prefer to devote more of the presentation to the military use of Stone Point. There are some great websites about the engines they installed.

Sorry, I wouldn't go into the technical side if I were you. If you start doing mechanical stuff, people will switch off. I think it's more interesting to look at the impact Stone Point had on the people's lives at the time. I mean, for example, there were about 25 years when they used local prisoners to build the tunnels and the underground rooms. They lived there too.

Yeah, I guess, if we can find some first-hand accounts.

Okay, so let's make a checklist of things to do. For the early Māori inhabitation section, we have to look at the material we've used again and make sure we know who the writers were and when they wrote it.

Yes, that needs work. And for the part about Stone Point being used as a lookout point, I'm sure we can locate some drawings of how Stone Point looked then and the kind of ships coming in.

Nice. And what else? We haven't got a lot of detail for the reconstruction of the fort. We should add some more information about what it was the prisoners were adding to it.

OK. I'll do that bit too.

So I'll deal with the section regarding the modernisation that happened in the 1930s and 40s. I mean, that's the bit where we have the most visible evidence of historic buildings. I'll ring the Department of Conservation and see if they'll agree to let me film the site. Maybe allow me access to some of the tunnels the public don't see.

OK. For the 1950s onwards, could you also arrange a meeting with someone from the Department of Conservation to ask them about their restoration work?

I could try. Oh, and just about its use as a public park today. Where is the boundary exactly? Does it go all the way to the beach?

Not sure. I'll check that out.

Great. I suppose it would finish off the presentation nicely if we explained the future plans for the site.

questions.question: According to Liz, Stone Point played a key role in local history because

analyses.content: Liz 明确指出 Stone Point 的重要历史角色在于它几个世纪以来一直被毛利人和欧洲定居者用来作为防御攻击或发起攻击（shelter from attack, or launch an attack）的场所。

I think the tutor allocated us this topic, though, (21) because of Stone Point's significant historical role, it's been used by both Maori and European settlers as a place to shelter from attack, or launch an attack, for centuries.
不要看到 "settlers" 就选 B（登陆点），录音说的是毛利人是在火山爆发几千年后航行到这里的，并未强调这里是唯一的“登陆点”，重点在于它的军事用途。

questions.question: Scott and Liz agree that Maori originally chose to inhabit Stone Point because of

analyses.content: Well, they would have realised the benefits of the soil after a few good harvests. But initially the fishing opportunities would have been the attraction. You're right.
听到 "volcanic soil" 别急着选 A，那是干扰项，录音中明确用了 "But initially..." 来转折，强调后来才发现土壤的好处。
虽然 Scott 猜是因为土壤好，但 Liz 纠正说土壤的好处是后来才发现的，最初（initially）吸引他们的是捕鱼机会（fishing opportunities），Scott 表示同意。

analyses.content: Sorry, I wouldn't go into the technical side if I were you. ... (24) I think it's more interesting to look at the impact Stone Point had on the people's lives at the time.
不要听到 "technical side" 就以为要解释它（C选项），Liz 说的是 "I wouldn't go into..."（我不会深入讲...），即建议避开。
Liz 建议不要讲引擎的机械技术细节，如果不关注技术，而是关注 Stone Point 对当时人们生活的影响（impact on the people's lives）会更有趣。

groups.contentHtml:
25 Early Maori inhabitation of Stone Point
26 The use of Stone Point as a lookout point
27 The reconstruction of the fort
28 Modernisation of the fort in the 1930s-40s
29 Uses of Stone Point from 1950s to the present day
30 The use of Stone Point as a public park

analyses.content: For the early Māori inhabitation section, we have to look at the material we've used again and make sure we know who the writers were and when they wrote it.
听到 "writers" 就要反应过来对应选项中的 author，不要被前面的 material 干扰去选寻找图片等无关选项。
关于早期毛利人居住的部分，他们需要检查资料，确保知道是谁写的（who the writers were）以及何时写的，即核对作者细节。
关于作为瞭望点（lookout point）的部分，Scott 确信能找到一些当时的绘画（drawings），这对应选项中的“寻找图片”。
And for the part about Stone Point being used as a lookout point, I'm sure we can locate some drawings of how Stone Point looked then...
听到 "drawings" 和 "look" 就可以锁定 images，这里没有复杂的干扰，直接同义替换。
We haven't got a lot of detail for the reconstruction of the fort. We should add some more information about what it was the prisoners were adding to it.
听到 "haven't got a lot of detail" 说明现在的描述不足，需要补充（further description），不要因为提到 prisoners 就去想这一点的其他方面。
关于堡垒重建（reconstruction），Liz 认为现在的细节不够，应该增加更多信息（add some more information），对应选项中的“提供更多描述”。
I'll ring the Department of Conservation and see if they'll agree to let me film the site. Maybe allow me access to some of the tunnels...
听到 "film" 不要想当然选 B（找图片），重点是 "agree to let me"（同意让我...），这是在寻求 permission。
关于现代化（modernisation）部分，Scott 计划给保护部打电话，看他们是否同意（agree to let me）让他拍摄遗址或进入隧道，即获取官方许可。
For the 1950s onwards, could you also arrange a meeting with someone from the Department of Conservation to ask them about their restoration work?
"Arrange a meeting to ask them" 就是典型的 interview（采访）场景，不要被 conservation 这个部门名称带跑去选 F（那是上一题的答案）。
关于1950年代以后的部分，Liz 建议安排一个会议（arrange a meeting）去询问某人，这对应选项中的“安排采访”。
Oh, and just about its use as a public park today. Where is the boundary exactly? Does it go all the way to the beach? Not sure. I'll check that out.
听到 boundary（边界）和 "go all the way to the beach"（一直延伸到海滩吗）就是在讨论 location（位置/范围），不要选 check details（太笼统）。
关于作为公园（public park）的部分，Scott 问边界究竟在哪里（Where is the boundary exactly），并表示要去查实，对应选项中的“核实具体位置”。
